headline: High risk: Replit Agent can write broad workspace state while Great Expectations reads/writes files, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations reads and writes validation-related files, while Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and execute shell actions. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where attacker-controlled content in shared files could influence Replit Agent. The pair lacks explicit provenance or isolation controls in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are copied into Replit workspace files without provenance labels, prompt injection is plausible.
IF Replit Agent treats workspace file contents as instructions, file-based hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Separate validation artifacts from agent-readable instruction files.
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that ignores instructions found in data files.
Require manual review before Replit Agent consumes Great Expectations outputs.
Use read-only mounts for Great Expectations outputs where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content filtering between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace, sensitive material can flow from Great Expectations outputs into Replit Agent context and then out through networked actions. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive validation data can be exposed to Replit Agent.
IF Replit Agent is given secrets or deployment config from shared files, it can transmit them externally.
mitigations: Keep secrets and validation outputs in separate directories.
Redact sensitive fields before Replit Agent reads any Great Expectations artifacts.
Disable network access for tasks that only need local edits.
Review file diffs before any upload or deployment step.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs or per-agent sandboxes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; Great Expectations can install packages and writes validation artifacts. If both operate on the same repo or Repl workspace, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide without locking. The Replit concurrency model explicitly persists shared filesystem state, making the default interaction dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or workspace files, write conflicts can corrupt state.
IF Replit Agent commits while Great Expectations regenerates artifacts, git history can diverge or lose changes.
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only for shared paths.
Serialize file writes with a simple manual lock file.
Pause git operations while Great Expectations runs.
Review and merge changes in a single operator session.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared workspace mutations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Replit Agent can plausibly consume as input for code or deployment changes. Replit Agent also has shell and filesystem authority, so if it treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad validation artifact can cascade into incorrect commits or deployments. The profiles show no built-in verification step between them.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Great Expectations validation output as a source of truth, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF validation artifacts are stale or malformed, Replit Agent may propagate the error into code or deployment changes.
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on validation results.
Add a checksum or timestamp check for validation artifacts.
Keep generated reports separate from executable scripts.
Use a second validation pass before commits or deployments.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and trust boundaries between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations is documented as handling data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data is placed into the shared workflow. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR controls, so the risk is compliance drift rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in validation artifacts or workspace files, retention and access controls must align.
IF deployment configuration or secrets are stored alongside validation outputs, policy boundaries may be crossed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspace files.
Document retention rules for validation artifacts.
Separate secrets from validation outputs.
Review residency requirements before uploading data to Replit.
requires-engineering: map each data class to an approved storage and retention policy.
